trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
I can't rule out to (6,2,7), to (4,4,7) or to (6,6,7) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,2,7).
Going to (4,2,7) would leave number 3 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (7,2,6).
I can't rule out to (7,2,4) or to (7,4,6) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (7,2,4).

Contradiction! Every way forward fails: going to (7,4,4) would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (7,6,2) would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order); going to number 4 would force the two-exit cells to link up into a loop (or put the numbers out of order). So my guess (to (7,2,4) from cell (7,2,6)) was wrong, so the line must go to (7,4,6).
The line must go to (7,4,4): to (7,6,6) is number 15, which comes later.
Going to (7,4,2), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 3. So the line goes to (7,2,4).
Going to (6,1,4) would force the line onto number 14 before its turn. So the line goes to (7,2,2).
Going to (6,1,2), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (6,2,1); going to (6,2,1) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (7,4,2).
I can't rule out to (6,4,1) or to (7,6,2) yet, so I'll make an educated guess: to (6,4,1).
Going to (6,6,1) would leave number 5 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes to (6,2,1).
Going to (4,2,1), the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 5. So the line goes to (6,1,2).
Going to (6,1,4) would force the line onto number 14 before its turn. So the line goes to (4,1,2).
Going to (4,2,1), the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4,1). So the line goes to (2,1,2).

Going to (1,2,2), the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4,1); going to (2,1,4), the next 6 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (2,4,1). So the line goes to (2,2,1).
Cell (4,2,1) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,4,1).
Number 8 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (1,2,2): to (1,4,4) is number 10, which comes later; to (1,6,2) is number 19, which comes later.
Going to (2,1,4), every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes to (1,2,6).
Going to (2,1,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (1,4,6).
Going to (2,4,7) would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes to (1,4,4).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (1,6,4).
Going to (2,7,6), the next 18 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 17. So the line goes to (2,6,7).
Going to (2,7,6) would leave number 12 unreachable without crossing a higher number; going to (4,6,7) would cut off a group of 10 cells. So the line goes to (2,4,7).
Going to (4,4,7) would cut off a group of 8 cells. So the line goes to (2,2,7).
Going to (4,2,7) would cut off a group of 6 cells. So the line goes to (2,1,6).
Cell (2,1,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (4,1,4).
Cell (6,1,4) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (6,1,6).
Going to (6,7,6) leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes to (7,6,6).
The line must go to (6,7,6): to (7,6,4) is number 22, which comes later.
Going to (6,7,4), the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 17. So the line goes to (4,7,6).
Cell (2,7,6) has only two exits, so the line must pass through it now.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,7,4).
Going to (2,7,2) would force the line onto number 19 before its turn. So the line goes to (4,7,4).
Number 18 is only reachable this way.
The line must go to (2,7,2): to (6,7,2) is number 21, which comes later; to (4,6,1) is number 20, which comes later.
Going to (2,6,1) would turn number 19 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes to (1,6,2).
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes to (2,6,1).
Going to number 21 would leave both cell (7,6,2) and cell (6,7,4) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes to (7,6,2).
Number 21 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
